London Liquidity / IFVG by Shujat
Roboquant
Strategy
Official

378 downloads
30 favorites
Added 2 weeks ago
The London session (an Eastern Time window) is tracked as a box of its high and low, and when it closes those two levels are drawn as lines. Inside a separate liquidity-sweep window, a close beyond the London high followed by a large-bodied candle (body over half its range) closing back inside marks a bearish sweep; the mirror move at the London low marks a bullish one. The strategy collects the fair value gaps that form during the session or after the sweep, and when price closes through one in the opposite direction, an inverse FVG that agrees with the sweep, it enters: short after a high sweep, long after a low sweep, with at most one setup per day. The stop is an ATR multiple or the recent swing, and the target is an ATR multiple, a Risk:Reward multiple or the opposite London level. Size is fixed contracts, a fixed dollar risk or a percentage of equity at the stop, and an optional filter limits trading to chosen weekdays. This showcase run uses the MNQ 5m preset: London box 03:30-09:25 ET, sweeps and entries between 09:25 and 13:15 ET, gaps up to 10 hours old, an ATR(14) stop at 2x and target at 0.2x, $1,000 risked per trade, and every weekday traded.

Per-bar strategy returns regressed on the symbol's buy-and-hold. Beta ≈ 0 with positive alpha = genuine edge; beta ≈ 1 = you're mostly holding the market. PSR = probability the true Sharpe exceeds 0 after correcting for sample length, skew and fat tails.
